collection.description: Every dance a villager dances turns into jumping.

ask.text:
Every dance (subject) dances turns into jumping. (subject.He/She) can't help it. Thirty hops at a time, round and round the fire, until everyone else has to stand back. The elders have started calling (subject.him/her) the Frog, not unkindly. Tonight is the harvest dance, and (subject) has been asked to lead it, which has never happened before.
Just before the drums start, (elder) takes (subject) aside. "The harvest dance is slow," (subject.he/she) says. "Stamp and sway. If you hop, the old ones will try to keep up, and someone will break a hip." Then (subject.he/she) smiles. "But it's your dance now."
Should (subject) dance it the old, slow way, or (subject.his/her) own way?

c1o1.text: Halfway through, something changes. The slow stamp gets into (subject)'s feet and stays there, and the itch to hop just isn't there any more. (subject.He/She) dances the whole harvest dance slow, and the next one, and the one after that. The elders stop calling (subject.him/her) the Frog. (subject.He/She) misses it, a little.

c1o2.text: It is the best harvest dance anyone can remember. The old ones dance longer than they have in years, because nobody is making them hop. At the end, (elder) hugs (subject) and says it was perfect. Then, at the very end, when the elders have sat down, (subject) does thirty hops round the fire on (subject.his/her) own, and everyone cheers.

c1.text: The drums start, slow and deep. (subject) stamps, and sways, and holds the hops in with every muscle (subject.he/she) has. Round the fire behind (subject.him/her), the old ones follow, swaying, smiling...

c2o1.text: The young ones love it. The old ones try to keep up. Halfway round, (elder) hops once too often and comes down badly. The healers say (subject.his/her) hip will mend. (elder) says from (subject.his/her) mat, "It was your dance. And it was worth it." (subject) dances slow at the next harvest.

c2o2.text: The old ones don't try to hop. They clap. They clap the beat for the young ones, laughing, and the young ones hop round them in a ring, and it's a new dance entirely, and everyone loves it. (subject) is so happy that a few things (subject.he/she) used to sulk about stop seeming to matter.

c2.text: The drums start slow. (subject) waits one beat, two, then gives the drummers a look, and the drums speed up, and (subject) starts to hop...
